title: leül and felül: Sitting Down, Sitting Up

sections.title: The same fel-/le- pair, on a new base verb
sections.content: ül ('to sit') is a simple, regular verb. Add le- and you get leül ('to sit down', moving from standing into a seat); add fel- and you get felül ('to sit up', moving from lying down into a sitting position). Same up/down logic as felkel and lefekszik, just a different everyday movement.

items.english: Károly sits down on the chair.
I wake up, and I sit up in bed.
Are you sitting up, or are you still lying down?

sections.content: leül naturally reaches for -ra/-re, the 'onto a surface' case from Unit 6 — leül a székre, leül a padra — because sitting down means moving onto something. felül works the same way when it means climbing onto something instead of just sitting up: felül a biciklire ('gets on the bike').
